tasks.prompt: Order the morning start up sequence for a small conventional surface water plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small conventional plant in western Canada starting production for the day after an overnight shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant at rest through steady treated water production to the clearwell.

cards.label: Review the overnight log, alarms, and clearwell level before starting any equipment
Inspect the raw water intake and confirm raw water is available at the plant inlet
Start chemical feed systems and confirm each pump is delivering at its set rate
Start the raw water pump and fill the rapid mix and flocculation basins at a low rate
Bring the filters online one at a time and confirm filtered water turbidity is on target
Raise plant flow to the normal rate and record start up flows, levels, and residuals

tasks.explanation: A safe start up checks records and stored water first, proves chemical feed before raw water moves, and only raises flow once filtered water quality is confirmed.

tasks.prompt: Order the planned evening shutdown sequence for a seasonal water treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional seasonal plant in a western Canadian recreation community shutting down at the end of the operating season.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant in normal production through the plant secured for the off season.

cards.label: Fill treated water storage to the planned shutdown level before reducing production
Reduce plant flow gradually and take the filters out of service one at a time
Stop chemical feeds and flush the feed lines with clean water
Drain exposed process piping that could freeze during the off season
Isolate and lock out pumps and drives that will not run during the shutdown
Complete the shutdown log and confirm alarms and monitoring are set for the off season

tasks.explanation: A planned shutdown protects stored water first, stops chemistry before water stops moving, drains freeze prone piping, and ends with lockout and a complete log.

tasks.prompt: Order the full conventional treatment train from raw water intake to finished water storage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada treating a prairie reservoir source with conventional treatment and chlorine disinfection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reservoir intake through treated water leaving the plant clearwell.

cards.label: Intake screening removes coarse debris at the raw water intake
Rapid mix disperses coagulant through the raw water
Flocculation gently builds large settleable floc
Sedimentation settles floc by gravity in the clarifier
Granular media filtration polishes the settled water
Chlorine disinfection and clearwell storage complete the finished water

tasks.explanation: The conventional train screens, coagulates, flocculates, settles, filters, and disinfects in that order, and only then stores finished water.

tasks.prompt: Order the direct filtration train for a consistently low turbidity mountain source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada on a low turbidity mountain stream source, approved for direct filtration without sedimentation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screened raw water through disinfected finished water.

cards.label: Screening removes coarse debris from the raw water
Coagulant is added and dispersed in the rapid mix
Brief flocculation forms small pin floc
Water passes directly to the granular media filters
Filters remove the floc and fine particles from the water
Chlorine disinfection follows filtration and finished water flows to storage

tasks.explanation: Direct filtration has no sedimentation step, so coagulation, brief flocculation, and the filters must carry the full particle removal load before disinfection.

tasks.prompt: Order the groundwater treatment train for iron and manganese removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional groundwater plant in western Canada treating well water with dissolved iron and manganese.
tasks.configuration: Scope: well water through aeration, oxidation, and filtration to storage.

cards.label: Well pump delivers raw groundwater to the plant
Aeration adds oxygen and strips dissolved gases from the water
Chemical oxidant is added and detention allows iron and manganese to oxidize
Oxidized iron and manganese form solid particles
Granular media filtration removes the oxidized particles
Chlorine disinfection and storage complete the treated water

tasks.explanation: Dissolved iron and manganese must be oxidized into solid particles with aeration, chemical oxidation, and detention time before filtration can remove them.

tasks.prompt: Order the shift handover sequence between outgoing and incoming operators.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional two operator plant in western Canada changing shifts at the end of a production day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: outgoing operator finishing the shift through the incoming operator taking charge.

cards.label: Outgoing operator completes the daily log with flows, doses, and any abnormal events
Outgoing operator walks the plant with the incoming operator and points out equipment status
Both operators review chemical tank levels, clearwell level, and active alarms together
Incoming operator confirms sampling completed and samples still outstanding
Incoming operator signs the handover record and takes charge of the plant
Outgoing operator reports any unresolved issue to the operator in charge before leaving

tasks.explanation: A good handover moves information in a fixed order, records first, then a joint walkthrough and level checks, and ends with a signed transfer of charge.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily plant walkthrough inspection routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 1 operator in western Canada completing the morning walkthrough of a small treatment plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entering the plant through recording the walkthrough findings.

cards.label: Check the plant entrance, security, and building heat and ventilation first
Inspect chemical storage and feed areas for leaks, levels, and containment condition
Check each treatment process for normal water levels, flows, and unusual sounds or odours
Read and record key flows, levels, pressures, and analyzer values
Test treated water chlorine residual and turbidity and compare with the online readings
Record all findings in the daily log and report anything abnormal to the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: The walkthrough moves from building safety to chemicals to processes, then verifies instruments with grab results before anything is logged as normal.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to return a raw water intake to service after a planned outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional river intake in western Canada returning to service after a planned maintenance outage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: intake isolated and inspected through raw water flowing to the plant.

cards.label: Inspect the intake screen and structure and confirm debris has been cleared
Confirm the intake pipe and wet well are full and free of trapped air
Open the intake isolation valve slowly to admit raw water
Start the raw water pump at a low rate and check for leaks and abnormal vibration
Flush the first raw water to waste until turbidity and appearance are normal
Raise raw water flow to the normal rate and record the return to service

tasks.explanation: An intake returns to service only after inspection, slow filling, a low rate pump start, and flushing the first water to waste until it looks normal.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily clearwell operating sequence from start of production to steady supply.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada with a single clearwell supplying the community distribution pumps.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clearwell level management through a normal production day.

cards.label: Confirm the clearwell level is above the minimum needed for disinfection contact time
Start filtration at a rate matched to the expected demand for the day
Verify the chlorine residual leaving the clearwell meets the plant target
Start distribution pumping to match community demand
Cycle the clearwell level between its low and high set points through the day
Record levels, residuals, and treated volumes in the daily log

tasks.explanation: Clearwell operation protects contact time first by holding the minimum level, then balances filtration inflow against distribution outflow while levels and residuals are logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence used to turn over water in a ground level treated water reservoir.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional community in western Canada with a ground level reservoir showing an aging chlorine residual.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a full draw down and refill cycle for water age control.

cards.label: Check the reservoir level trend and the chlorine residual at the reservoir sample point
Plan the draw down for a low demand period so system pressure is protected
Draw the reservoir down to its low operating level through normal demand
Refill the reservoir with freshly treated water at a controlled rate
Confirm the residual in the refilled reservoir has recovered to the target
Record the turnover volumes and residuals in the operating log

tasks.explanation: Turnover replaces aged water with fresh treated water, timed to low demand, and the refill is proven by residual recovery before the cycle is logged complete.

tasks.prompt: Order the source water changeover sequence between the duty well and the river intake.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada that can draw from a well or a river intake, switching from the well to the river for a planned well outage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: well supplying the plant through the river intake supplying the plant steadily.

cards.label: Confirm the river intake is available and raw river quality has been checked
Run a jar test on the river water and set the treatment doses for the new source
Start the river raw water pump at a low rate and flush the intake line to the plant
Blend or switch the plant feed from well water to river water gradually
Stop the well pump once the plant is stable on river water and secure the well
Monitor treated quality closely through the changeover and record the switch in the log

tasks.explanation: A source changeover prepares chemistry for the new water before it arrives, flushes the idle line, switches gradually, and only secures the old source once the plant is stable on the new one.

tasks.prompt: Order the jar test procedure used to select a coagulant dose.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bench jar test on the current raw water at a plant in western Canada, using six jars and a range of alum doses.
tasks.configuration: Scope: collecting the raw water sample through choosing the dose for the plant.

cards.label: Collect a fresh raw water sample and measure its turbidity, pH, and alkalinity
Fill each jar with the same measured volume of raw water
Add a different coagulant dose to each jar while rapid mixing
Rapid mix briefly to disperse the coagulant evenly
Slow mix to simulate flocculation and let floc form
Stop mixing, allow a set settling period, then measure settled turbidity and select the lowest dose that meets the target

tasks.explanation: A jar test mirrors the plant in miniature: identical raw water in every jar, a dose range added during rapid mix, then flocculation, settling, and a turbidity comparison to pick the dose.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical addition sequence at the rapid mix of a conventional plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada adjusting alkalinity and feeding alum plus a polymer aid on a low alkalinity prairie source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw water entering the rapid mix through the flocculation basin inlet.

cards.label: Measure raw water pH, alkalinity, and turbidity before dosing
Add alkalinity supplement first where raw alkalinity is too low for coagulation
Add the primary coagulant at the point of maximum turbulence
Allow rapid mix to disperse the coagulant before any aid is added
Add polymer coagulant aid downstream of the rapid mix
Carry the dosed water into gentle flocculation

tasks.explanation: Coagulation chemistry is set in order: confirm the raw water, correct low alkalinity, disperse the primary coagulant at maximum turbulence, then add the aid where it can build floc.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to place a flocculation basin into service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional three stage tapered flocculation basin in western Canada being returned to service after cleaning.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty flocculation basin through normal operation at design flow.

cards.label: Inspect paddles, drives, and baffles and confirm the basin is clean
Fill the basin slowly with water from upstream
Start the paddle drives at the lowest speed setting
Introduce coagulated water from the rapid mix
Set the tapered speeds, highest in the first stage and lowest in the last
Observe floc size at the basin outlet and adjust speed or dose as needed

tasks.explanation: A flocculation basin is filled and started gently, with tapered mixing that is strongest where floc is forming and gentlest where finished floc must not be sheared.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to take a flocculation basin out of service for cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional flocculation basin in western Canada being removed from service for its annual cleaning.
tasks.configuration: Scope: basin in normal service through the basin drained and ready for cleaning crews.

cards.label: Shift plant production to the remaining treatment train and confirm capacity
Stop coagulated water flow into the basin and close its inlet valve
Stop the paddle drives once flow into the basin has stopped
Drain the basin contents to the residuals handling system
Wash down walls, paddles, and baffles and remove settled solids
Inspect paddles, drives, and baffles while the basin is empty and record the findings

tasks.explanation: Cleaning preparation protects plant production first, stops flow and drives in order, drains to residuals handling, and uses the empty basin to inspect equipment.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to place a sedimentation basin into service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional rectangular sedimentation basin in western Canada returned to service after a cleaning outage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clean empty clarifier through steady settled water flow to the filters.

cards.label: Inspect the basin, sludge collectors, and effluent weirs and confirm they are clean and level
Fill the basin slowly to avoid disturbing the inlet baffles
Start the sludge collection mechanism before flow is introduced
Introduce flocculated water at a reduced flow rate
Raise flow gradually to the normal rate once a sludge blanket forms
Check settled water turbidity at the effluent weir before sending full flow to the filters

tasks.explanation: A clarifier is filled slowly, its sludge collector runs before solids arrive, and flow is raised gradually so the blanket and settled water quality are established before full production.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleaning sequence for a sedimentation basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional annual cleaning of a rectangular clarifier in western Canada with accumulated sludge and algae growth.
tasks.configuration: Scope: basin in service through the cleaned basin ready to refill.

cards.label: Shift production to the remaining basins and confirm plant capacity
Close the influent and effluent valves to isolate the basin
Drain the basin to the residuals handling system
Wash down walls, weirs, and baffles and remove the remaining sludge
Inspect the sludge collector, weirs, and surface coating while the basin is empty
Close the drain and record the basin as ready for a controlled refill

tasks.explanation: Basin cleaning isolates and drains the cell to residuals handling, washes and inspects it while empty, and leaves it ready for the slow controlled refill used at start up.

tasks.prompt: Order the sludge blanket monitoring and removal sequence for a clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada checking a clarifier whose settled water turbidity has started to rise.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first sign of rising settled turbidity through blanket control restored.

cards.label: Measure settled water turbidity and compare it with the normal plant range
Measure the sludge blanket depth at several points across the basin
Check the sludge withdrawal rate and the solids content of the withdrawn sludge
Increase the sludge withdrawal rate if the blanket is deeper than the target range
Recheck blanket depth and settled turbidity after the adjustment has taken effect
Record blanket depths, withdrawal rates, and turbidity results in the process log

tasks.explanation: Blanket control starts with measurement, not adjustment: turbidity and blanket depth are confirmed first, withdrawal is changed, and the result is remeasured before it is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response when raw water turbidity rises sharply during spring runoff.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada on a river source entering spring runoff with rapidly rising raw turbidity.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first detection of the turbidity rise through stable treatment at the new conditions.

cards.label: Confirm the turbidity rise with a grab sample and check the raw water pH and alkalinity
Run a quick jar test series on the new raw water to reset the coagulant dose
Adjust the coagulant and aid feeds to the jar test dose before the poor water reaches the filters
Reduce plant flow if settled water turbidity cannot be held on target
Monitor settled and filtered turbidity closely and increase sludge withdrawal as solids load rises
Record the runoff conditions, doses, and results and notify the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: Runoff response resets chemistry with a fresh jar test before the poor quality water works through the plant, uses flow reduction as the backup control, and keeps close monitoring until treatment is stable.

tasks.prompt: Order the settled water quality check routine after a coagulant dose change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada verifying the effect of a coagulant dose increase made one hour earlier.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dose change already made through confirming or correcting the new dose.

cards.label: Note the time of the dose change and allow one basin detention time to pass
Collect a settled water sample at the clarifier effluent weir
Measure settled water turbidity, pH, and colour and compare with plant targets
Observe floc carryover and the appearance of the clarifier surface
Trim the coagulant dose in a small step if settled quality is off target
Record the results and the final dose in the process log for the next operator

tasks.explanation: A dose change is judged only after the changed water has travelled through the basin, and settled turbidity, pH, and appearance together decide whether a further small trim is needed.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence for switching coagulant feed from the duty tank to the standby tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional alum feed system in western Canada with duty and standby bulk tanks, the duty tank near empty.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duty tank running low through the standby tank feeding the plant.

cards.label: Confirm the standby tank level, product identity, and that its suction line is clear
Note the current feed rate and the time so the changeover is recorded accurately
Open the standby tank suction valve before closing the duty tank valve
Close the duty tank suction valve once the pump is drawing from the standby tank
Confirm steady feed by a calibration column drawdown on the new supply
Record the changeover, both tank levels, and the confirmed feed rate in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: A tank changeover never starves the pump: the new supply is proven and opened first, the old supply is closed second, and delivery is confirmed by drawdown.

tasks.prompt: Order the full backwash sequence for a gravity granular media filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional rapid gravity filter in western Canada at the end of a run, washed with air scour and filtered water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter taken out of service through the end of the wash cycle.

cards.label: Close the filter influent valve and let the water level draw down
Close the filter effluent valve to isolate the filter from the clearwell
Open the waste drain valve to the backwash waste line
Start air scour to loosen the media bed
Start the backwash pump and raise wash water flow gradually
Wash until the waste water runs clear, then stop the pump and close the drain

tasks.explanation: Backwashing isolates the filter first, opens the waste path before any wash water flows, uses air scour to loosen deposits, and ends only when the waste water runs clear.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to return a freshly backwashed filter to service using filter to waste.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional rapid gravity filter in western Canada that has just been backwashed and must ripen before production.
tasks.configuration: Scope: end of backwash through the filter going into full production.

cards.label: Allow the media bed to settle and the water above it to clear after backwashing
Open the influent valve and start filtration at a reduced rate to the waste line
Run filter to waste while effluent turbidity falls during ripening
Confirm filtered water turbidity meets the plant target on a grab sample or analyzer
Close the waste valve and open the effluent valve to the clearwell
Raise the filtration rate gradually to the normal production rate

tasks.explanation: A backwashed filter ripens as the bed re forms its removal layer, so the first filtered water goes to waste until turbidity meets the target, and only then is the filter put into production.

tasks.prompt: Order the planned shutdown sequence for a gravity filter cell.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter in western Canada being removed from service for a week of underdrain repairs.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter in production through a drained and secured filter cell.

cards.label: Reduce plant flow or shift production to the remaining filters
Close the filter influent valve to stop flow into the cell
Close the filter effluent valve to isolate the cell from the clearwell
Open the drain and lower the water level to just above the media
Drain the remaining water slowly so the media bed is not disturbed
Lock out and tag the filter valves and record the shutdown in the log

tasks.explanation: A planned filter shutdown first protects plant production, then isolates the cell on both sides, drains it slowly to protect the media, and finishes with lockout and a log entry.

tasks.prompt: Order a filter media inspection during a drained filter outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional inspection of a dual media filter in western Canada suspected of mudball formation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter drained for inspection through the inspection findings recorded.

cards.label: Drain the water to just below the media surface
Take core samples of media at several points across the bed
Measure the media depth and compare it with the design depth
Check the cores for mudballs, fouling, and media loss or mixing
Inspect the exposed underdrain and support gravel where visible
Record depths and findings and set the corrective work before refilling

tasks.explanation: A media inspection samples the bed itself: cores reveal mudballs and fouling, depth checks reveal media loss, and findings are recorded before the filter is returned to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter run monitoring routine used through a production day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada monitoring two gravity filters through a normal production day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start of the filter run through the decision to backwash.

cards.label: Record the starting headloss and filtered water turbidity for each filter
Check headloss and turbidity at the set interval and plot the trend through the run
Watch for a turbidity rise that signals the start of breakthrough
Watch for headloss approaching the plant limit that signals a clogged bed
End the run when turbidity, headloss, or run time reaches its plant limit, whichever comes first
Record the run length and the reason for ending the run in the filter log

tasks.explanation: A filter run is managed by trend, not by clock alone: headloss and turbidity are tracked together and the run ends at the first limit reached.

tasks.prompt: Order the slow sand filtration train from intake to finished water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small system in western Canada using slow sand filtration on a clean source water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screened raw water through the slow sand beds and disinfection.

cards.label: Intake screening removes coarse debris
Pre filtration or roughing filtration reduces the load on the beds
Slow sand beds develop a biological layer on the sand surface
Water percolates slowly through the sand and the biological layer
Filtered water receives chlorine disinfection
Finished water flows to storage

tasks.explanation: Slow sand filtration relies on the biological layer that forms on the bed surface, so the beds run slowly and continuously, and disinfection still follows filtration.

tasks.prompt: Order the membrane filtration train from intake to finished water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada using low pressure ultrafiltration membranes after coagulation pretreatment.
tasks.configuration: Scope: river intake through membrane permeate disinfection and storage.

cards.label: Intake screening removes coarse debris
Coagulant is mixed into the raw water as pretreatment
Flocculation forms floc ahead of the membranes
Membrane modules separate solids from the permeate by size exclusion
Permeate receives chlorine disinfection for a distribution residual
Finished water flows to clearwell storage

tasks.explanation: Membranes physically separate particles from the permeate, but a chlorine residual is still added after membrane filtration because membranes provide no lasting disinfectant residual.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response when filtered water turbidity rises above the plant target.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter in western Canada showing a steady filtered turbidity rise midway through a run.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first confirmed rise through the filter restored or removed from service.

cards.label: Confirm the rise with a grab turbidity sample to rule out an analyzer fault
Check settled water turbidity to see if the load from upstream has increased
Check the filtration rate and reduce it if the filter is running above its normal rate
Inspect the filter surface and effluent for signs of breakthrough or media upset
Take the filter out of service and backwash it if turbidity keeps rising
Record the event, the checks made, and the outcome in the filter log and notify the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: A turbidity response verifies the reading first, then works upstream to downstream, rate, settled quality, and bed condition, and removes the filter from service if quality cannot be recovered.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting sequence when a filter backwash is not cleaning the bed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter in western Canada whose headloss stays high after washing and whose waste water never ran dirty.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a completed wash that left the bed dirty through the confirmed root cause check.

cards.label: Review the backwash flow rate record against the design wash rate
Confirm the backwash pump delivered full flow for the full wash duration
Check that the air scour ran for its full set time before the water wash
Inspect the drained bed surface for mudballs and cracking
Check the wash water troughs and waste valve for partial blockage or leakage
Correct the cause found and repeat a supervised wash to confirm cleaning

tasks.explanation: A wash that does not clean is diagnosed in order: wash rate, pump delivery, air scour, bed surface, and waste path, and the fix is proven with a supervised repeat wash.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to bring a new filter into service after media replacement.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional gravity filter in western Canada refilled with new sand and anthracite after a media replacement.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new media placed in the cell through the filter entering normal production.

cards.label: Inspect the underdrain and support gravel before any new media is placed
Place the support gravel and media in layers to the design depths and level the surface
Fill the filter slowly from below to avoid disturbing the new bed
Backwash the new media repeatedly until the waste water runs clear and fines are removed
Run filter to waste and confirm filtered turbidity meets the plant target
Place the filter into normal production and record the new media details in the asset record

tasks.explanation: New media is commissioned from the bottom up: underdrain first, careful layered placement, gentle filling, repeated washing to remove fines, and a filter to waste proof before production.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a sodium hypochlorite feed system for disinfection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional sodium hypochlorite feed system in western Canada starting with the plant for the day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: day tank check through a confirmed residual at the clearwell outlet.

cards.label: Check the hypochlorite day tank level and the age and strength of the solution
Open the suction and discharge valves and prime the metering pump
Start the feed pump paced to plant flow at the calculated dose
Confirm feed by a calibration column drawdown
Measure the free chlorine residual after the contact point
Adjust the dose so the clearwell outlet residual meets the target

tasks.explanation: Hypochlorite feed is proven at the pump by drawdown and proven in the water by the measured residual, with the dose trimmed only after both checks are known.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for collecting a distribution chlorine residual sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional routine free chlorine residual check at a designated sample station in a western Canadian community.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving at the sample tap through recording the result.

cards.label: Select the designated sample tap and remove any aerator or hose
Flush the tap at a steady flow for several minutes to draw fresh main water
Rinse the sample cell with the sample water
Fill the cell and add the DPD reagent for free chlorine
Read the residual in the colorimeter within the method time limit
Record the result, location, date, and time in the sampling log

tasks.explanation: A residual sample must represent the main, not the plumbing, so the tap is flushed first, the cell is rinsed with sample, and the DPD reading is taken within the method time.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence an operator follows to confirm chlorine contact time compliance for the day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada disinfecting with free chlorine through a baffled clearwell, following provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gathering the operating data through recording the contact time result.

cards.label: Record the lowest clearwell water level and the corresponding contact volume
Determine the peak flow rate through the contactor for the period
Calculate the theoretical detention time from volume divided by peak flow
Apply the baffling factor to get the effective contact time
Measure the free chlorine residual at the contactor outlet and record temperature and pH
Multiply residual by effective contact time and compare the result against the required value for the target inactivation

tasks.explanation: Contact time compliance is residual multiplied by effective contact time, so volume at its lowest level, peak flow, and the baffling factor must all be fixed before the measured residual is applied.

tasks.prompt: Order the bench procedure to determine chlorine demand on a raw water sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bench test in western Canada measuring the chlorine demand of a river water sample after runoff.
tasks.configuration: Scope: collecting the sample through reporting the demand value.

cards.label: Collect a fresh sample and record its temperature, pH, and turbidity
Fill a set of sample bottles with the same measured volume
Dose each bottle with a different known chlorine dose and mix
Hold the bottles in the dark for the set contact period
Measure the free chlorine residual remaining in each bottle
Calculate demand as dose minus residual for the bottle that holds the target residual and record the result

tasks.explanation: Demand is what the water consumes, so identical samples receive a dose range, share the same contact period, and demand is calculated from the residual that remains.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up sequence for an ultraviolet disinfection unit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada using ultraviolet disinfection ahead of chlorine addition for a residual.
tasks.configuration: Scope: UV unit at rest through validated disinfection at normal flow.

cards.label: Inspect the UV reactor and confirm the quartz sleeves and wipers are clean
Fill the reactor with water and confirm there are no leaks and no trapped air
Power the lamps and allow the full warm up period before admitting full flow
Confirm lamp intensity and ultraviolet transmittance readings are in the normal range
Open flow through the reactor gradually to the normal rate
Confirm the calculated dose is on target and record intensity, flow, and dose in the log

tasks.explanation: An ultraviolet unit must be clean, full of water, and fully warmed up with intensity proven before flow is raised, because dose depends on intensity, transmittance, and flow together.

tasks.prompt: Order the chlorine gas cylinder changeover sequence at a small plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small plant in western Canada using chlorine gas cylinders with a trained operator and the plant safety procedure in place.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duty cylinder empty through the fresh cylinder feeding the chlorinator.

cards.label: Put on the required protective equipment and confirm the emergency equipment is in place and a second trained person is present
Close the empty cylinder valve and the chlorinator supply valve
Purge and disconnect the empty cylinder and cap its outlet
Connect the fresh cylinder with a new gasket and open its valve briefly to check for leaks with the approved leak test
Open the supply to the chlorinator and confirm chlorine feed has resumed
Tag the empty cylinder, secure both cylinders, and record the changeover in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: A gas chlorine changeover puts people and emergency readiness first, isolates and caps the empty cylinder, leak tests the new connection before feed resumes, and ends with cylinders secured and logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the residual monitoring routine for treated water storage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada checking residuals at the clearwell, reservoir, and a distant sample station on a weekly round.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning the round through recording and acting on the results.

cards.label: Review the last set of residual results and note any location trending downward
Collect the clearwell outlet residual first as the plant reference value
Collect the reservoir residual and record the reservoir level at the time of sampling
Collect the distant sample station residual after a full tap flush
Compare each result with the plant target and with the clearwell reference
Report any low residual location to the operator in charge and record all results in the log

tasks.explanation: Storage monitoring works outward from the plant reference value, so losses through storage and distance can be seen clearly and any low location is reported the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a chlorine booster station in the distribution system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional hypochlorite booster station in western Canada returning to service after maintenance.
tasks.configuration: Scope: booster station isolated through a confirmed raised residual downstream.

cards.label: Confirm the hypochlorite tank level and that suction and discharge lines are intact
Prime the metering pump and confirm feed by a calibration drawdown
Measure the incoming residual upstream of the booster station
Start the booster feed at the calculated setting for the target downstream residual
Measure the residual at the downstream check point after the mixing time has passed
Trim the feed to hold the target and record doses and residuals in the station log

tasks.explanation: A booster station is set from the incoming residual, proven at the pump by drawdown, and confirmed downstream only after the boosted water has had time to mix and travel.

tasks.prompt: Order the disinfection and commissioning sequence for a new watermain.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional new subdivision watermain in western Canada, disinfected following provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: installed and pressure tested main through final clearance to place it in service.

cards.label: Flush the new main to remove debris and dirty water
Fill the main with chlorinated water to the target chlorine dose
Hold the chlorinated water in the main for the required contact period
Flush the main until the chlorine residual matches the distribution system
Collect bacteriological samples on two consecutive days and receive absent results
Connect the main to the live system and place it in service

tasks.explanation: A new main is cleaned, disinfected with a held chlorine dose, flushed back to system residual, and only connected after consecutive absent bacteriological results.
